scenario.name: Palo Alto Unit 42, Huntress & SentinelOne — INC Ransom & Lynx: Citrix NetScaler Exploitation, wmic.exe Distributed DLL Execution & MEGASync Double Extortion
scenario.overview: Picture a wide multi-lane city highway approaching an overhead exit sign gantry and a row of striped toll plaza booths with automated lifting barrier arms. Cruising down the multi-lane express highway, a driver mounts a cloned electronic toll transponder behind the windshield right before entering the fast-pass lane. In this real-world scenario, the intruder smuggles copied records out past the overhead license-plate gantry in tiny disguised batches, then smuggles copied records out past the overhead license-plate gantry in tiny disguised batches. The highway authority’s overhead license-plate camera spots two different vehicles using the same toll pass minutes apart and sounds an immediate toll-plaza alert. In this scenario (T1046, Palo Alto Unit 42, Huntress & SentinelOne, INC Ransom & Lynx: Citrix NetScaler Exploitation, wmic.exe Distributed DLL Execution & MEGASync Double Extortion), the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: edge Appliance Compromise, NetScan Discovery, then mass WMIC /node:@"hosts.txt" DLL, then aES-128-CTR + Curve25519 Encryption. Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering Edge Appliance Compromise, NetScan Discovery, then Mass WMIC /node:@"hosts.txt" DLL, then AES-128-CTR + Curve25519 Encryption, while the Process Hierarchy tab keeps the Parent → Child spawn tree visible so you can see which trusted process launched the next payload. Primary detection correlates Sysmon Event 22 with the documented host and network chain.

stages.title: Stage 2: Mass WMIC `/node:@"hosts.txt"` DLL Distribution & `rundll32.exe` Execution
stages.subtitle: Lateral Movement & Execution (T1047 - WMI / T1218.011 - Rundll32)
stages.description: As the car rolls beneath the overhead highway gantry, the toll booth reader recognizes the cloned pass signal and automatically lifts the striped barrier arm. Here in Step 2 inside the highway toll plaza, the intruder smuggles copied records out past the overhead license-plate gantry in tiny disguised batches without disturbing the local side-road ramp. After copying the ransomware DLL (inc.dll or lynx.dll) to \\<host>\C$\Windows\Temp\ across every IP in hosts.txt, the operator executes a single wmic.exe command that remotely spawns rundll32.exe on every machine in the enterprise simultaneously (logged in Sysmon Event 1 with MassDeploymentCommand=wmic.exe /node:@"hosts.txt" process call create, DllLoader=rundll32.exe C:\Windows\Temp\inc.dll,Main, MitreTechnique=T1047 , WMI + T1218.011 , Rundll32 so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes wmic.exe /node:@"C:\Windows\Temp\hosts.txt" /user:"CORP\DomainAdmin" /password:"*" process call create "rundll32.exe C:\Windows\Temp\inc.dll,Main --fast" (which executes Microsoft's signed rundll32.exe host binary to load a target DLL into memory and directly invoke its exported function entrypoint , wmic.e so that proxies execution of malicious DLL code , T1047 through a trusted, Microsoft-signed system binary during "Mass WMIC /node:@"hosts.txt" DLL Distribution & rundll32.exe Execution" to evade application allowlisting and process-name heuristics). On the diagram, follow Step #2 / Link #2 (#2→ wmic.exe /node:@"C:\Windows\Temp\hosts.txt" process call create "rundll32.exe C:\Windows\Temp\inc.dll,Main --fast" / ⇠#2 ACK 1) from Node ② (#2 Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap) to Node ③ (#3 Citrix NetScaler / Edge VPN Foothold), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Domain Endpoints (rundll32 inc.dll -> .INC / .LYNX)).

keySpecs.value: Block `wmic.exe /node:` remote process creation across workstation and server subnets via Windows Firewall (DCOM port 135) and alert on `wmiprvse.exe` spawning `rundll32.exe`.
Lateral Movement & Execution (T1047 - WMI / T1218.011 - Rundll32)

stages.title: Stage 3: AES-128-CTR + Curve25519 Encryption, Wallpaper Change & Network Printer Ransom Notes
stages.subtitle: Impact (T1486 - Data Encrypted for Impact / T1491.001 - Internal Defacement)
stages.description: The vehicle accelerates smoothly through the express toll lane onto the restricted city bypass while every ordinary commuter waits in the cash queue next door. In this final step inside the highway toll plaza, the intruder smuggles copied records out past the overhead license-plate gantry in tiny disguised batches until the highway toll camera log catches the mismatch. Both INC Ransom and Lynx encrypt files using AES-128-CTR paired with Curve25519 elliptic-curve key exchange (.INC or .LYNX), change the Windows desktop wallpaper to the ransom notice, and call EnumPrintersW + WritePrinter to automatically print the physical ransom note on every connected office network printer (logged in Sysmon Event 11 with RansomwareFamily=INC Ransom / Lynx , Shared C++ Source Code, PrinterExtortion=EnumPrintersW + WritePrinter physical ransom note printing, EncryptedExtension=.INC / .LYNX so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes rundll32.exe C:\Windows\Temp\lynx.dll,Main (AES-128-CTR + Curve25519 encryption -> *.LYNX & README.txt) (which executes Microsoft's signed rundll32.exe host binary to load a target DLL into memory and directly invoke its exported function entrypoint , rundll so that proxies execution of malicious DLL code , T1486 through a trusted, Microsoft-signed system binary during "AES-128-CTR + Curve25519 Encryption, Wallpaper Change & Network Printer Ransom Notes" to evade application allowlisting and process-name heuristics). Next, the follow-up artifact winspool.drv!EnumPrintersW() -> OpenPrinterW() -> WritePrinter(hPrinter, szRansomNote...) runs (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , winspool.drv!EnumPrintersW, -> OpenPrinterW, -> WritePrinter, hPrinter, szRansomNote... vi so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1486 during "AES-128-CTR + Curve25519 Encryption, Wallpaper Change & Network Printer Ransom Notes" , Both INC Ransom and Lynx encrypt files using AES-128-CTR paired with Curve25519 elliptic-curve key exchange , while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). On the diagram, follow Step #3 / Link #3 (#3→ rundll32.exe / ⇠#3 ACK 11) from Node ③ (#3 Citrix NetScaler / Edge VPN Foothold) to Node ④ (#4 Admin Host (wmic.exe /node:@hosts.txt)), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Domain Endpoints (rundll32 inc.dll -> .INC / .LYNX)).
